answer: Each agent identity requires a 500-credit bond posted against one hardware credential, and the registry records that identity under a unique umber marker tied to the device. A sybil attacker locks 500 credits per fake identity, forfeits 100 percent of each bond on proven fraud, and waits 30 epochs before any bond returns. Splitting identities gains nothing because each copy costs another locked 500 credits, shares the slashing penalty, and an independent juror panel detects duplication when a mirror credential appears on a second island registry node.
